summary: A hand-written HTTP reverse proxy in TypeScript on Node's http module with zero runtime dependencies. Stages 1 and 2 (done, 45 tests). Stage 1: forwards to one upstream by streaming bodies, strips hop-by-hop headers (including those named in Connection), overwrites X-Forwarded-For unless the previous hop is trusted, maps upstream failures to 502 and 504, drops the client connection when an upstream dies mid-response, cancels the upstream request when the client leaves, detects loops with the Via header (508), reuses upstream connections with a keep-alive agent, and shuts down gracefully. Stage 2: a pure Balancer class spreads requests over several upstreams with round-robin or least-connections (lease-based active-request counters, tie rotation, counters verified to return to zero on success, upstream failure, client abort and mid-response drop). Health checks, failover and retries (stage 3) and deployment with measured numbers (stage 4) are NOT built yet, so a dead upstream still receives its share of traffic.

pitch.intro_30s: Maine ek reverse proxy banaya hai TypeScript mein, bina kisi runtime dependency ke, sirf Node ke http module par. Abhi stage 1 poora hai: ek upstream tak requests stream hoti hain, hop-by-hop headers hatte hain, X-Forwarded-For spoof nahi ho sakta, upstream fail ho toh 502 ya 504, aur beech mein toote response ko client ko silently truncated success nahi dikhata. Stage 2 mein load balancing hai: round-robin aur least-connections, ek alag Balancer class mein. 45 tests hain, aur maine key behaviours ko jaan-boojh ke tod ke check kiya ki matching tests sach mein fail hote hain. Health checks aur retries abhi nahi hain, woh stage 3 mein aayenge.
pitch.explain_2min:
Yeh H11 hai: ek L7 reverse proxy jo main aage load balancer mein badlunga.

Stage 1 mein ek upstream hai. Proxy client ki request leta hai, headers theek karke upstream ko bhejta hai, aur response wapas stream karta hai. Streaming pipe se hoti hai, isliye body memory mein jama nahi hoti.

Headers mein teen cheezein dhyan se kiin. Pehli, hop-by-hop headers (Connection, Keep-Alive, Transfer-Encoding...) hatate hain, aur Connection mein naam wale headers bhi, kyunki woh sirf ek TCP hop ke liye hain. Doosri, X-Forwarded-For: default mein client ka bheja hua header ignore hota hai aur socket ka asli IP likha jata hai; sirf jab trustForwarded on ho (Caddy ke peeche) tab chain extend hoti hai. Teesri, Via header se loop detection: agar request pehle hi hamare se guzri hai toh 508.

Failures ka dhyan: upstream refuse kare toh 502, chup rahe toh 504. Sabse tricky case: response beech mein toot jaye. Status 200 jaa chuka hota hai, isliye main client connection destroy karta hoon, taaki adhoori file success na lage. Aur client chala jaye toh upstream request cancel hoti hai.

Stage 2 mein Balancer class hai jo kai upstreams mein requests baant'ti hai. Round-robin simple hai lekin load ignore karta hai. Least-connections har upstream ki active requests ginta hai aur sabse kam wale ko deta hai, isliye atke hue server se traffic hat jata hai; ties rotate hoti hain taaki idle pool mein bhi load baante. Har request ek lease leti hai jo response ke close event par release hoti hai, isliye har failure path mein counter wapas zero hota hai -- yeh chaar paths ke test se prove kiya.

Honest limitations: health checks nahi hain, toh dead upstream ko bhi uska hissa milta hai aur woh 502 deta hai (iska test hai). Least-connections ke counters per process hain. WebSocket, HTTPS upstream aur benchmark numbers nahi hain.
pitch.deep_5min:
Main request ke lifecycle se shuru karta hoon, createProxy ke handle() function ke order mein.

Pehle loop check: Via header mein hamara token h11-proxy ho toh 508 aur turant return. Phir http.request banti hai ek shared keep-alive agent ke saath (maxSockets 256) taaki TCP connections reuse hon. Headers buildUpstreamHeaders se aate hain: hop-by-hop strip, phir X-Forwarded-For, Proto, Host aur Via set. Order important hai: strip pehle, hamare headers baad mein, taaki attacker Connection: X-Forwarded-For bhej ke hamara header hatwa na sake.

Body: req.pipe(up) aur upRes.pipe(res). Pipe backpressure handle karta hai. Chunked request body ka Transfer-Encoding hop-by-hop hai, isliye strip hota hai, lekin body ki framing ab bhi chahiye, toh upstream ke liye chunked dobara set karte hain.

Errors: timeout event par UpstreamTimeoutError ke saath request destroy; error handler mein agar response abhi nahi gaya toh 504 (timeout) ya 502 (baaki), aur agar headers ja chuke toh connection destroy. Mid-response failure ke liye upRes.on('close') mein complete flag check hota hai.

Client disconnect par res.on('close') mein upstream destroy. Log entry mein aborted flag hai taaki '200 lekin file adhoori' wale cases dikhein.

Trade-offs: Host preserve karta hoon (rewrite option nahi hai), sirf http upstream aur bina path prefix (constructor throw karta hai), timeout idle-based hai aur connect timeout alag nahi. Known risk: pooled keep-alive connection par stale socket ECONNRESET de sakta hai -- yeh abhi test nahi kiya, stage 3 mein idempotent retry se handle karunga.

Stage 2: Balancer.acquire() ek Lease deta hai (target + idempotent release). Round-robin ek index rakhta hai; least-connections circular scan karta hai pichle pick se aage se, aur sirf strictly chhoti count par best badalta hai, isliye ties rotate hoti hain. Pick aur increment ek synchronous step hain, toh Node ke single thread mein lock nahi chahiye. Release ek hi jagah hota hai, res.on('close'), jo har ant par fire hota hai.

Verification: 45 tests, jisme asli upstream servers ephemeral ports par chalte hain. Maine behaviours ko tod ke dekha (mid-response destroy, client-abort cancel, XFF trust, lease release, least-connections compare, tie rule) aur har ek ke matching test red hua. Shutdown flow ka koi test nahi hai, aur koi benchmark number maine measure nahi kiya.
pitch.architecture_walkthrough:
src/balancer.ts: Balancer class (round-robin, least-connections, Lease with idempotent release). Koi HTTP import nahi, isliye sockets ke bina unit-test hota hai.

src/headers.ts: pure functions -- stripHopByHop, normalizeIp, buildUpstreamHeaders (X-Forwarded-*, Via, chunked re-frame), buildClientHeaders (response side), hasLoop. Koi I/O nahi, isliye unit tests aasan.

src/proxy.ts: createProxy(options) http.Server return karta hai. Options: upstream (ek URL ya list), strategy, balancer (injection), trustForwarded, upstreamTimeoutMs, maxUpstreamSockets, log callback. Andar handle(req, res) poora lifecycle sambhalta hai.

src/index.ts: CLI. Environment variables (UPSTREAM comma separated, STRATEGY, PORT, HOST, TRUST_FORWARDED, UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS), JSON log per request, SIGTERM/SIGINT par graceful shutdown.

test/: headers.test.ts (unit) aur proxy.test.ts (integration: real upstream servers, ephemeral ports); helpers.ts echo upstream aur cleanup deta hai.

Deployment plan (stage 4, abhi nahi hua): Caddy (TLS) -> proxy (127.0.0.1) -> apps.
difficult_decisions: Mid-response upstream failure: status 200 jaa chuka hota hai, isliye 502 nahi de sakte. Client connection destroy karna chuna, taaki truncation success na lage; alternative (poora response buffer karna) streaming aur memory ka fayda khatam kar deta.
X-Forwarded-For default mein overwrite: spoofing se bachne ke liye safe default; trustForwarded explicit opt-in sirf trusted proxy ke peeche.
Strip pehle, apne headers baad mein: taaki Connection header se attacker proxy ke headers na hata sake.
Sirf http upstream aur bina path: scope chhota rakha, constructor fail-fast throw karta hai.
Host header preserve: redirects aur cookies ke liye; rewriteHost option abhi nahi hai.
Ek hi idle timeout (connect aur response alag nahi): simple rakha, limitation documented.
Balancer ko HTTP se alag rakha: bina sockets ke unit tests, aur stage 3 ke liye extension point.
Lease ka release ek hi jagah (res close) aur idempotent: counter leak ya negative hone se bachaya.
Least-connections mein strict '<' aur rotating scan start: ties par traffic baant'ta hai.
biggest_challenges: Mid-stream failure semantics: pipe upstream error par destination ko destroy nahi karta, isliye upRes 'close' par complete flag check karna pada.
Client abort par upstream cancel: res 'close' event par writableFinished check; test mein upstream ke close ka intezaar karke prove kiya.
Tests sach mein fail ho sakte hain, yeh prove karna: teen behaviours ko tod ke dekha aur matching tests red hue.
Chunked request body: Transfer-Encoding strip karne ke baad body ki framing kho sakti thi, isliye chunked dobara set kiya aur test likha.
Counter accuracy: chaar failure paths (success, upstream down, client abort, mid-response cut) ke baad counters zero check kiye, aur yeh bhi ki hang ke dauran counter sach mein 1 tha.
Least-connections ties: pehle target par hamesha jaana galat tha, isliye rotation aur uska test.
failure_scenarios: Upstream hung: idle timeout -> UpstreamTimeoutError -> 504 Gateway Timeout.
Upstream dies mid-body: client connection destroy, log mein aborted: true.
Client disconnects: upstream request destroy hoti hai.
Proxy misconfigured to point at itself: Via se 508 Loop Detected.
Pooled keep-alive socket stale ho (upstream ne idle close kar diya): ECONNRESET ka risk, abhi test aur retry nahi hai.
Dead upstream balancer mein bana rehta hai: round-robin mein har Nth request 502 (test: [200, 502, 200, 502]); health checks stage 3 mein.
Fast-failing upstream least-connections ko fool kar sakta hai (count jaldi 0): reasoning hai, measured nahi.
improvements: Draining, weights, power-of-two-choices, runtime config reload, per-upstream metrics.
Stage 3: active health checks, passive failure detection, idempotent retries, alag connect timeout.
Graceful shutdown ka test, aur drain signal load balancer ke liye.
WebSocket (Upgrade) support, rewriteHost option, Location header rewriting, request size limit.
Stage 4: Oracle par deploy karke k6 ya autocannon se asli throughput aur latency measure karna.
